description: MySQL topology and options: version, replicas, replication mode, ProxySQL.

fields.name: version
fields.description: Server series; packages come from repo.mysql.com.
fields.title: MySQL version

fields.name: replicas
fields.description: Secondary servers besides the primary; with Group Replication the whole group is primary + replicas and may not exceed 9 members.
fields.title: Replicas

fields.name: replication
fields.description: async = classic binlog replication; semi_sync = the semisync plugin waits for one replica ack; group = Group Replication (its own consensus, no semisync).
fields.title: Replication mode

fields.name: single_primary
fields.description: Group Replication mode: on = one writable primary with automatic election, off = multi-primary (every member writable).
fields.title: Single-primary group

fields.name: semi_sync_wait_for_slave_count
fields.description: rpl_semi_sync_source_wait_for_replica_count: how many replicas must acknowledge before the primary commits.
fields.title: Semi-sync acks

fields.name: proxysql
fields.description: ProxySQL instances routing reads and writes to the right member; 0 = clients talk to the primary directly.
fields.title: ProxySQL nodes

fields.name: init_sql
fields.description: SQL executed on the primary once the server is up, before the workload.
fields.title: Init SQL

rules.message: Group Replication needs 3..9 members, i.e. replicas between 2 and 8
semi-synchronous and Group Replication both need at least one replica
cannot wait for more acks than there are replicas
ProxySQL in front of a single server only adds a hop
